records.table: Westland Flagship is the standing single malt of Westland in Seattle: five malts with a touch of peated malt, married from new oak, former bourbon and oloroso casks. It brings custard, nougat and toasted marshmallow at 46 per cent, and took American Oak's place in 2021.
records.story: Westland began in Seattle in 2010, by its own timeline, with the aim of a single malt as distinct as the Northwest that made it, not a copy of Scotch; its stills first ran in 2011. In 2013 the distillery opened in the SoDo district, its copper stills in view of visitors, and released its first whiskey. For some years its standing range was three bottlings: American Oak, Sherry Wood and Peated. In December 2016 Rémy Cointreau agreed to buy the distillery, and the purchase was completed in January 2017. In the spring of 2021 the house ceased making the three and drew on its stocks for one bottling in their place: Westland Flagship, five malts with a little peated malt from Scotland, married from new and used American oak, former bourbon and former oloroso casks for at least 40 months and bottled at 46 per cent. It folds the three old bottlings into one, so a guest who remembers American Oak, Sherry Wood or Peated is poured the Flagship, and it is the bottle to reach for when a guest asks what American single malt tastes like.

records.table: From the Denver distillery that has made single malt since 2004, Stranahan's Original American Single Malt Whiskey is the standing bottle: all malted barley in new charred oak at 94 proof, with caramel, butterscotch and spiced pear.
records.story: A barn fire brought the founders together, as the house tells it. In 1998 a volunteer firefighter came to a burning barn on a ranch at Woody Creek, near Aspen, and met its owner, a physicist who had founded the Flying Dog brewery. The two became friends, and in 2004 they set up a whiskey distillery in Denver, the whiskey named for the rancher. The early spirit was distilled from Flying Dog's beer, though the accounts differ on how. Its early bottles were labelled Stranahan's Colorado Whiskey, and Stranahan's is widely called the first licensed whiskey distillery in Colorado since Prohibition. In 2009 the distillery moved into a former brewery building on South Kalamath Street in Denver, and in 2010 Proximo Spirits bought the business, saying the whiskey would stay where it was. In time the bottling came to be labelled Original American Single Malt Whiskey, and from January 2025 the category had a federal standard of its own. Guests ask for it as the Rocky Mountain malt, and in the glass it shows what new charred oak does to malted barley.

records.table: McCarthy's Oregon Single Malt Whiskey is the peated malt of Clear Creek Distillery, first released in 1996, long before American single malt had a federal standard: Scottish peated barley, one pass through a pot still and three years in Oregon oak.
records.story: Steve McCarthy (died 2023) founded Clear Creek Distillery in Portland in 1985 to make eaux-de-vie from Oregon fruit, pear above all, in the European manner. A taste for peated Scotch, found on a trip to Scotland as the story goes, set him on a malt of his own. He brought in peated malted barley from Scotland, had it brewed into a wash, ran it once through a Holstein pot still and laid it down in barrels of Oregon oak. McCarthy's Oregon Single Malt was released in 1996, years before American single malt was spoken of as a category, and its maker says the American Single Malt Whiskey Commission recognises it as the first of the kind. In 2014 McCarthy sold Clear Creek to Hood River Distillers and stayed on to advise, and in 2017 Hood River Distillers announced that the distillery's work would move from Portland to Hood River. He died in January 2023, at 79. The malt kept its Scottish peat, its single pass and its three years in Oregon oak. Where American single malt began is in this bottle, and so is the answer for a guest who wants a smoky malt made in the United States.

records.story: Two partners started House Spirits Distillery in Corvallis, Oregon, in 2004, and soon moved it to Portland. Whiskey takes years, and the house first made its name with gin: Aviation American Gin, worked out with a bartender. The malt grew meanwhile under the Westward name and was made the brewer's way: a wash of Northwest two-row barley brewed and fermented on site, distilled twice in pot stills and aged in full-size new American oak barrels, heavily toasted and lightly charred. In time came stout cask, cask strength and other finishes. In April 2025 House Spirits filed for Chapter 11 protection, and in October 2025 a court approved the sale of most of its assets to the private investors who had financed it through the case. Brewed, distilled and aged in one Portland distillery, Westward makes plain that an American single malt begins as beer.

records.table: Virginia Distillery Co. makes its single malt at Lovingston in the Blue Ridge foothills, and Courage & Conviction Signature Malt is its flagship: all malted barley from bourbon, sherry and red wine casks, bottled at 46 per cent, with raspberry jam, caramel and spice.
records.story: In 2011 a businessman who wanted a malt distillery of his own in the Blue Ridge foothills of Nelson County founded Virginia Distillery Co. A pair of copper pot stills made in Scotland was set at Lovingston. The founder died while the distillery was being built, and his family carried the work on. The distillery opened in 2015, and its own malt was laid down in bourbon, sherry and red wine casks. In 2020 it released Courage & Conviction, named for a saying the founder often repeated: the distillery's own single malt, aged at least three years, a marriage of the three casks at 46 per cent. Single cask bottlings of each wood came after it, and in January 2025 its category gained a federal standard. It carries American single malt well beyond the West: a Virginia malt in the Scottish manner, its red wine casks giving it a colour of its own.
